answer: A gale of fake agents hits hardest at a network's nadir, when honest users are fewest and sockpuppets tip every vote. A sequential VDF identity mint stops that cold. Each new agent must compute a verifiable delay function taking six hours on one CPU core before its identity activates, and anyone checks the proof in milliseconds. Minting 10,000 sockpuppets takes 60,000 CPU-hours and $4,800 in cloud compute, while one honest agent pays nothing but patience. Like a falcon circling before it dives, every identity earns its wings slowly, so mass forgery arrives too late and too broke.
